title: Literary Attribution & Theme Framing: Alkotása, témája, megtestesítője

sections.title: Framing European Literary Masterworks
sections.content: In both the Hungarian citizenship and cultural knowledge examinations (*Magyar kulturális ismereti vizsga*), literary works are linked to their creators and central themes using possessive attribution (*Homérosz eposza*, *Shakespeare tragédiája*) and genitive role nouns (*a felvilágosodás kiemelkedő alakja*, *a tudásvágy megtestesítője*).

sections.title: Official Exam Roster: Antiquity to Goethe (Explained)
rows: Ancient Greek epics: the Iliad depicts the siege of Troy and Achilles' wrath; the Odyssey chronicles Odysseus' 10-year perilous journey home to Ithaca.
William Shakespeare: Rómeó és Júlia, Hamlet
English Renaissance tragedies: Romeo and Juliet portrays young lovers torn apart by family hatred; Hamlet explores moral duty, revenge, and conscience ('Lenni vagy nem lenni').
17th-century French classicist comedies exposing human greed (Harpagon) and religious hypocrisy (Tartuffe) with sharp wit.
18th-century French Enlightenment philosophical satire questioning blind optimism ('minden a lehető legjobb világon') through Candide's misadventures.
German dramatic poem: the ageing scholar Faust makes a wager with Mephistopheles (the devil) in search of ultimate knowledge and meaning — directly inspiring Imre Madách.

items.spanish: Homérosz két világhírű eposza, az Iliász és az Odüsszeia az európai irodalom bölcsője.
items.english: Homer's two world-famous epics, the Iliad and the Odyssey, are the cradle of European literature.

items.spanish: Shakespeare tragédiáit Arany János és Vörösmarty Mihály ültette át mesteri magyar nyelvre.
items.english: Shakespeare's tragedies were translated into masterful Hungarian by János Arany and Mihály Vörösmarty.

items.spanish: Goethe Faustja az örökké küzdő és tudásra szomjazó ember jelképe.
items.english: Goethe's Faust is the symbol of the eternally striving human thirsting for knowledge.
